status: Local declaration before the material-grid calculation, not external preregistration. Previous project outputs were already known.
question: Under which declared material and volume assumptions can a low-density crust support a specified remanent magnetization?
density_uncertainty_rule: Deterministic sensitivity bands; no Gaussian distribution, joint covariance, posterior or probability of feasibility is assumed.
carrier: Magnetite only, nonmagnetic matrix and pores. Carrier fraction f is by solid volume inside the source; no other carriers or matrix remanence.
remanence_source: Dunlop & Arkani-Hamed 2005, Table 3: SD magnetite TRM 5–10 kA/m at 50 microtesla. This is a domain-state scenario, not a measured Martian crust calibration. Saturation magnetization is not used.
field_scaling: Linear weak-field scaling to 5 microtesla is a declared approximation, not a new experimental calibration.
effective_carrier_remanence: M50*(B/50)*preservation_efficiency; coherence multiplies once after acquisition. Efficiency 0.1 is a sensitivity, not a measured loss.
volume_rule: All material has the same matrix and porosity. Only fraction q of the density averaging volume contains magnetite; the remaining fraction is the same porous nonmagnetic matrix. Density is an arithmetic volume average, not a gravity sensitivity kernel. M_source is per bulk source volume, and M_whole_volume=q*M_source.
calculation: Solve exact density and magnetization equations for every declared combination; report unconstrained candidates plus physical admissibility and cap screens. Compute exact attainable intervals over porosity and mineral caps, rather than relying on a coarse grid in f or phi.
application_to_tests_3_4: Read q10/q50/q90 of three base cylinder geometries plus thick20_centered_after_poisson_cancellation_chron_0.67_myr. Apply already penalized target with c=1 only, to avoid a second cancellation penalty. These are volume-assumption illustrations, not co-located density measurements or independent data.
decision: A combination fails if its candidate is unphysical or outside declared caps; a surviving combination establishes algebraic compatibility only. No universal rejection of low-density magnetic crust, mineral abundance inference, or geological probability from a sampled parameter fraction.
verification: Independent linear-program optimization of attainable ranges
Known dimensional example and rejection of unphysical inputs
Exactly one application of coherence; volume averaging q
limitations: Hemispheric density and local/deep magnetic-source support are not established to coincide.
Porosity up to 30 percent at depth is a stress test, not demonstrated stable deep crust.
Matrix density, field strength, grain state, alteration and vector geometry remain uncertain.
Uncertainty endpoints for density and prior depth products do not define joint probability distributions.
